newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges lower, cargo weak.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges lower, cargo weak.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges sank on Thursday with a major that was trying to push the market higher a few days earlier said offering at lower numbers, traders said.
High sulphur cargoes were weaker with little buying interest, while low sulphur cargoes were largely steady.
High sulphur fuel oil barges fetched as low as $81.50 a tonne fob ARA, or $2.50 below Wednesday's closing levels, and earlier trades were done at $82.25 and $82.
Some traders said $84 and $83.50 was done in the morning but others said it was just talk, not deals.
Late talk was around the $81 mark, trader said.

Some traders said the market was affected by the activity of a major that has stopped trying to push the market up as it did earlier this week. The major was said to be the cheapest seller at $83 in the morning.
"The major that was buying (higher) earlier this week is not anymore," one trader said.
Other traders pinned the weakness on weak demand and the crude complex weakness.
Low sulphur barges were offered at a steady $96 a tonne after a deal a day earlier at that number, but buyers were reported to be $2 to $3 lower.

"I am still offering at $96 (a tonne) and there is some buying interest but no deal has been done yet," the seller of Wednesday's cargo, a Rotterdam-based major, said, adding buying interest was coming in at $94.
A second trader said buyers were at $93.
High sulphur cargoes were weaker with little buying interest, although swaps gained a bit in the afternoon.
A Scandinavian refiner cut its offer price from $81 fob last week to a floating price equivalent to $77.50 fob.
"There's very low buying interest," the seller said.
A Russian cracked cargo was offered at slightly weaker numbers that Wednesday, at two means minus $1 and buyers were talking $1 lower.
One percent was largely steady as swaps recovered a little in the afternoon, with July offered at $91.50.
A refiner was still offering a low sulphur cargo at $94.50 fob. Three potential buyers were said to be at 50 cents to $1 lower.
A large low sulphur cargo traded at $94.75 late last week.
"I've got other restrictions which have nothing to do with price and that's why the deal is taking a bit of time," the refiner said.
-- Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom, +44 171 542 8145
